questions.q: One of the following regions has the world's largest tropical peatland, which holds about three years worth of global carbon emissions from fossil fuels; and the possible destruction of which can exert detrimental effect on the global climate. Which one of the following denotes that region?
questions.explain: The Congo Basin is home to the world's largest tropical peatlands, along with Brazil and Indonesia. The peat swamp forest of the Congo Basin stores around 29 billion tons of carbon – approximately equivalent to three years' worth of global greenhouse gas emissions – while the Basin as a whole absorbs nearly 1.5 billion tons of carbon dioxide a year.\n\nThe Basin stretches across six countries- Cameroon, Central African Republic, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Congo, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon.

questions.q: Invasive Species Specialist Group' (that develops Global Invasive Species Database) belongs to which one of the following organizations?
options: The International Union for Conservation of Nature
The United Nations World Commission for Environment and Development
The World Wide Fund for Nature
questions.explain: The Invasive Species Specialist Group is part of the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). This group is responsible for maintaining the Global Invasive Species Database, which helps in monitoring and managing species that threaten biodiversity on a global scale.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: Which of the following organisms perform waggle dance for others of their kin to indicate the direction and the distance to a source of their food?
questions.explain: The waggle dance is a specialized behavior of honeybees, used to communicate information about the direction and distance to a food source. This unique behavior allows other bees in the hive to find the food. Other species listed, such as butterflies, dragonflies, and wasps, do not exhibit this behavior.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: Which one of the following makes a tool with a stick to scrape insects from a hole in a tree or a log of wood?
questions.explain: In a study, researchers observed five captive, group-living Sumatran orangutans (Pongo pygmaeus abelii) using and creating tools to extract food from artificial mound holes. Three of the adult orangutans frequently stripped leaves and twigs from provided branches (tool-making) and then inserted these tools into the holes to access food (tool-using). If the tool didn’t fit into the hole, the orangutans typically modified it or adjusted their technique, such as altering their grip on the tool.

questions.q:
With reference to Gucchi sometimes mentioned in the news, consider the following statements :
1. It is a fungus.
2. It grows in some Himalayan forest areas.
3. It is commercially cultivated in the Himalayan foothills of north-eastern India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is correct: Guchhi mushroom is a species of fungus in the family Morchellaceae of the Ascomycota. One of the most sought-after edible mushrooms, guchhi is known for its spongy, honeycombed head and savoury flavour but all of that comes at a high price.\n\nStatement 2 is correct and Statement 3 is not correct: Apart from its flavour, guchhi also owes its high price to the challenges in cultivation. The mushrooms cannot be cultivated commercially and grow in conifer forests across temperature regions, and the foothills in Himachal Pradesh, Uttaranchal, and Jammu and Kashmir. And it takes months for villagers to collect enough of these mushrooms, dry them and bring them to the market.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a bird?
questions.explain: Option (a) is correct: Golden Mahseer is a fish, whose scientific name is Tor putitora. Mahseer roughly translates as mahi – fish and sher – tiger, and hence is also referred as tiger among fish. It is a large cyprinid and known to be the toughest among freshwater sport fish.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Moringa (drumstick trees) is a leguminous evergreen trees.
2. The Tamarind tree is endemic to South Asia.
3. In India, most of the tamarind is collected as minor forest produce.
4. India exports tamarind and seeds of moringa.
5. Seeds of moringa and tamarind can be used in the production of biofuels.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain:
Statement 1 is not correct: Drumstick is one of those rare plant species whose seeds, flowers, leaves, and stems are edible and extremely nutritious. Moringa, commonly referred to as drumstick, is treated as a 'super plant' for its unique yet powerful properties that combat different ailments in our system. This nutrient-dense plant has its roots in Ayurveda and was used as a medicine by our ancestors. Drumstick is an easily available vegetable which is cultivated mostly in Asian and African regions. It is a staple vegetable in Southern India. It can be evergreen and semi-deciduous.

Statement 2 is not correct: The tamarind tree is endemic to Tropical Africa.

Statement 3 is correct: In India, most of the tamarind is collected as minor forest produce.

Statement 4 is correct: India exports tamarind and seeds of moringa. Moringa has been in great demand in many countries. The major countries that import moringa leaves and seeds are the US, Germany, China, Canada, South Korea, and other European countries.

Statement 5 is correct: Seeds of moringa and tamarind can be used in the production of biofuels.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a filter feeder?
questions.explain: Oysters are filter feeders, meaning they eat by pumping large volumes of water through their bodies. Water is pumped through the oyster's gills. Plankton, algae, and other particles become trapped in the mucus of the gills. From there, these particles are transported to the oyster's mouth.

questions.q: Which one of the following is used in preparing a natural mosquito repellent?
questions.explain: Lemongrass acts as a natural mosquito repellent. It helps one to get rid of mosquitoes and keep them at bay. All you need to do is crush the leaves of lemongrass and then apply the oily mixture to your skin.

questions.q: With reference to India's biodiversity, Ceylon frogmouth, Coppersmith barbet, Gray-chinned minivet and White-throated redstart are
questions.explain: Ceylon frogmouth, Coppersmith barbet, Grey-chinned minivet, and White-throated redstart are birds. Coppersmith Barbet is a short, stocky bird, with a leaf-green body that allows it to remain well-camouflaged in the canopy. White-throated redstart is found in the Indian Subcontinent and Southeast Asia. Grey-chinned minivet is a small minivet species distributed in the Indian subcontinent and southeast Asia.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
With reference to Indian elephants, consider the following statements:
1. The leader of an elephant group is a female.
2. The maximum gestation period can be 22 months.
3. An elephant can normally go on calving till the age of 40 years only.
4. Among the States in India, the highest elephant population is in Kerala.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is correct: Indian elephants are highly social animals, gathering into matriarchal units. The leader of the group is the oldest female. Statement 2 is correct: The gestation period lasts for 22 months, yielding a single baby. Statement 3 is incorrect: An elephant can go on calving even after the age of 40 years. Statement 4 is incorrect: Among the states, the highest population was recorded in Karnataka (6,049), followed by Assam (5,719) and Kerala (3,054).
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Wildlife - Naturally found in
1. Blue-finned Mahseer : Cauvery River
2. Irrawaddy Dolphin : Chambal River
3. Rusty Spotted Cat : Eastern Ghats
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.explain: Pair 1 is correctly matched: Blue-finned Mahseer is found in the Cauvery river basin in Karnataka. Pair 2 is not correctly matched: The Irrawaddy dolphin is found in Chilika lake, Odisha, not in the Chambal River. Pair 3 is correctly matched: The rusty-spotted cat inhabits the forests of Andhra Pradesh and Eastern Ghats.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Some species of turtles are herbivores.
2. Some species of fish are herbivores.
3. Some species of marine mammals are herbivores.
4. Some species of snakes are viviparous.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: All statements are correct. Some turtle species are herbivores. Some fish species are herbivores. Some marine mammals (like manatees) are herbivores. Some snake species are viviparous, giving birth to live young instead of laying eggs.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Asiatic lions are naturally found in India only.
2. Double-humped camels are naturally found in India only.
3. One-horned rhinoceros are naturally found in India only.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is correct: Asiatic lions are naturally found only in India, in Gir National Park, Gujarat. Statement 2 is incorrect: Double-humped camels are found in India (Nubra Valley, Ladakh) and other parts of Central Asia. Statement 3 is incorrect: One-horned rhinoceros are found in India, Bhutan, Nepal, Indonesia, and Malaysia.

questions.q: The term sixth mass extinction/sixth extinction is often mentioned in the news in the context of the discussion of
options: Widespread monoculture practices in agriculture and large-scale commercial farming with indiscriminate use of chemicals in many parts of the world that may result in the loss of good native ecosystems.

Fears of a possible collision of a meteorite with the Earth in the near future in the manner it happened 65 million years ago that caused the mass extinction of many species including those of dinosaurs.

Large-scale cultivation of genetically modified crops in many parts of the world and promoting their cultivation in other parts of the world which may cause the disappearance of good native crop plants and the loss of food biodiversity.
Mankind's overexploitation/misuse of natural resources, fragmentation/loss of natural habitats, destruction of ecosystems, pollution, and global climate change.
questions.explain: The term sixth mass extinction/sixth extinction refers to the ongoing anthropogenic extinction event caused by human activities. It is characterized by mankind's overexploitation of natural resources, habitat destruction, pollution, and climate change, leading to an accelerated rate of species extinction.

questions.q: If you want to see gharials in their natural habitat, which one of the following is the best place to visit?
questions.explain: The best place to see gharials in their natural habitat is the Chambal River. Gharials are found in the river systems of India and Nepal, including the Chambal River (Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan), Girwa River (Uttar Pradesh), Son River (Madhya Pradesh), Gandak River (Bihar), and Mahanadi River (Orissa).

questions.q: In which of the following regions of India are you most likely to come across the 'Great Indian Hornbill' in its natural habitat?
options: Higher Himalayas of Jammu and Kashmir
questions.explain: The Great Indian Hornbill is most likely to be found in the Western Ghats. There are four species of hornbills in the Western Ghats, with the Great Indian Hornbill being the most prominent. They are also found in north and northeast India, as well as in Nepal, Bhutan, and Bangladesh.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
What is/are unique about 'Kharai camel', a breed found in India?
1. It is capable of swimming up to three kilometers in seawater.
2. It survives by grazing on mangroves.
3. It lives in the wild and cannot be domesticated.
questions.explain: The Kharai is a unique breed of camel found only in Kutch. They have the special ability to survive on both dry land and in the sea. They swim in seawater and feed on saline plants and mangroves. The Kharai can swim more than 3 km in search of mangroves for grazing. While they do live in coastal areas, they can be domesticated and are bred by local communities.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: Which one of the following is the national aquatic animal of India?
questions.explain: The Ganges River Dolphin is the national aquatic animal of India. This mammal represents the purity of the holy Ganga as it can only survive in pure and fresh water. It inhabits parts of the Ganges, Meghna, and Brahmaputra rivers in India, Nepal, Bhutan, and Bangladesh.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
With reference to 'dugong', a mammal found in India, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is a herbivorous marine animal.
2. It is found along the entire coast of India.
3. It is given legal protection under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
questions.explain: Dugongs are herbivorous marine mammals. They are protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. However, they are not found along the entire coast of India, but only in specific areas like the Gulf of Mannar, Palk Bay, Gulf of Kutch, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
With reference to Neem tree, consider the following statements:
1. Neem oil can be used as a pesticide to control the proliferation of some species of insects and mites.
2. Neem seeds are used in the manufacture of biofuels and hospital detergents.
3. Neem oil has applications in the pharmaceutical industry.
questions.explain: Neem oil can be used as a natural pesticide. It also has applications in the pharmaceutical industry due to its medicinal properties. However, neem seeds are not commonly used in the manufacture of biofuels or hospital detergents.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
Other than poaching, what are the possible reasons for the decline in the population of Ganga River Dolphins?
1. Construction of dams and barrages on rivers.
2. Increase in the population of crocodiles in rivers.
3. Getting trapped in fishing nets accidentally.
4. Use of synthetic fertilisers and other agricultural chemicals in crop fields in the vicinity of rivers.
questions.explain: The decline in Ganga River Dolphin population is attributed to habitat fragmentation by dams and barrages, indiscriminate fishing leading to accidental trapping, and pollution from agricultural runoff. Crocodiles are not a significant threat to dolphins.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
If you walk through the countryside, you are likely to see some birds stalking alongside the cattle to seize the insects disturbed by their movement through grasses. Which one of the following is/are such bird/birds?
1. Painted Stork
2. Common Myna
3. Black-necked Crane
questions.explain: The Common Myna is known to follow cattle and other large animals, feeding on insects disturbed by their movement. Painted Storks and Black-necked Cranes have different feeding habits and are not typically associated with this behavior.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
Consider the following fauna and India:
1. Gharial
2. Leatherback turtle
3. Swamp deer
Which of the above is/are endangered?
questions.explain: All three species - Gharial, Leatherback turtle, and Swamp deer - are endangered. Gharials are critically endangered, Leatherback turtles are vulnerable globally but critically endangered in some regions, and Swamp deer are listed as endangered on the IUCN Red List.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Star tortoise
2. Monitor lizard
3. Pygmy hog
4. Spider monkey
Which of the above are naturally found in India?
questions.explain: Star tortoises, monitor lizards, and pygmy hogs are naturally found in India. Spider monkeys are found in Central and South America, not in India.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
Consider the following animals:
1. Sea cow
2. Sea horse
3. Sea lion
Which of the above is/are mammal/mammals?
questions.explain: Sea cows (dugongs) and sea lions are mammals. Seahorses are fish, not mammals.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
In which of the following States is lion-tailed macaque found in its natural habitat?
1. Tamil Nadu
2. Kerala
3. Karnataka
4. Andhra Pradesh
questions.explain: The lion-tailed macaque is endemic to the Western Ghats of South India. It is found in its natural habitat in the states of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka. It is not found in Andhra Pradesh.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
The Government of India encourages the cultivation of 'sea buckthorn'. What is the importance of this plant?
1. It helps in controlling soil erosion and in preventing desertification.
2. It is a rich source of biodiesel.
3. It has nutritional value and is well-adapted to live in cold areas of high altitudes.
4. Its timber is of great commercial value.
questions.explain: Sea buckthorn helps prevent soil erosion and fixes nitrogen. It is not a significant source of biodiesel. It has nutritional value and is adapted to cold, high altitude areas. Its timber does not have great commercial value as it is a shrub, not a tree.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: Which one of the following groups of animals belongs to the category of endangered species?
options: Great Indian Bustard, Musk Deer, Red Panda and Asiatic Wild Ass
Kashmir Stag, Cheetal, Blue Bull and Great Indian Bustard
Snow Leopard, Swamp Deer, Rhesus Monkey and Saras (Crane)
Lion-tailed Macaque, Blue Bull, Hanuman Langur and Cheetal
questions.explain: Great Indian Bustard, Musk Deer, Red Panda, and Asiatic Wild Ass are all endangered species according to the IUCN Red List.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: What is the difference between the antelopes Oryx and Chiru?
options: Oryx is adapted to live in hot and arid areas whereas Chiru is adapted to live in steppes and semi-desert areas of cold high mountains.
Oryx is poached for its antlers whereas Chiru is poached for its musk.
Oryx exists in western India only whereas Chiru exists in north-east India only.
None of the statements (a), (b) and (c) given above is correct.
questions.explain: Oryx lives in arid regions with low rainfall, primarily in deserts and plains. Chiru is a Tibetan antelope that lives in cold high mountains.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
Which of the following can be threats to the biodiversity of a geographical area?
1. Global warming
2. Fragmentation of habitat
3. Invasion of alien species
4. Promotion of vegetarianism
questions.explain: Global warming, habitat fragmentation, and invasion of alien species are all significant threats to biodiversity. Promotion of vegetarianism is not typically considered a threat to biodiversity.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Black-necked crane
2. Cheetah
3. Flying squirrel
4. Snow leopard
Which of the above are naturally found in India?
questions.explain: Black-necked crane, flying squirrel, and snow leopard are naturally found in India. Cheetahs were declared extinct in India in 1952.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: Vultures which used to be very common in the Indian countryside some years ago are rarely seen nowadays. This is attributed to:
options: the destruction of their nesting sites by new invasive species
a drug used by cattle owners for treating their diseased cattle
scarcity of food available to them
a widespread, persistent and fatal disease among them
questions.explain: Vultures in India are on the verge of extinction due to the illegal use of a banned drug to treat cattle. The vultures eat the remains of the drugged animals and suffer kidney failure and visceral gout, which is usually fatal.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: A sandy and saline area is the natural habitat of an Indian animal species. The animal has no predators in that area, but its existence is threatened due to the destruction of its habitat. Which one of the following could be that animal?
questions.explain: The Indian wild ass (Equus hemionus khur) is found in the Little Rann of Kutch and surrounding areas in Gujarat. Its preferred environment is saline deserts (Rann), arid grasslands, and shrublands.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Biodiversity is normally greater in the lower latitudes as compared to the higher latitudes.
2. Along the mountain gradients, biodiversity is normally greater in the lower altitudes as compared to the higher altitudes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Both statements are correct. Biodiversity generally increases from poles to tropics, and decreases from lower to higher altitudes on mountains due to factors like temperature and seasonal variations.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
Biodiversity forms the basis for human existence in the following ways:
1. Soil formation
2. Prevention of soil erosion
3. Recycling of waste
4. Pollination of crops
questions.explain: All four statements are correct. Biodiversity contributes to soil formation, prevention of soil erosion, recycling of waste, and pollination of crops, all of which are essential for human existence.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a site for in-situ method of conservation of flora?
questions.explain: Botanical Garden is not a site for in-situ conservation of flora. In-situ conservation involves preserving species in their natural habitats, while botanical gardens are ex-situ conservation sites.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: The Himalayan Range is very rich in species diversity. Which one among the following is the most appropriate reason for this phenomenon?
options: It has a high rainfall that supports luxuriant vegetative growth.
It is a confluence of different biogeographical zones.
Exotic and invasive species have not been invasive species and have not been introduced in this region.
questions.explain: The Himalayas encompass three distinct biogeographical zones: the Northwest, West, Central, and East Himalayas. Together, these regions make up approximately 6.4% of India's total area. This region serves as a meeting point for various biogeographical zones, contributing to its extraordinary species diversity and making the Himalayas one of the richest areas in terms of biodiversity.
